ESSAY / ATTENTION

The Quiet Work of Paying Attention

In an age of acceleration, noticing has become a radical form of care.

By Mara Ellison · October 12, 2024 · 18 min read

“The world does not become richer when we move faster through it.”

— Simone Weil

There is a particular kind of tiredness that arrives when every moment has been accounted for. It is not the tiredness of work, exactly, but of being asked to witness everything at once.

Attention asks for less. It asks us to stay with the cup cooling beside the book, the late light gathering on the floor, the sentence we almost skipped.

A practice of staying

To pay attention is not to collect more impressions. It is to let one impression become precise.

The ordinary is not waiting to be made extraordinary. It is waiting to be met without haste.
